products.name: Rotten Apple Store
products.summary: A marketplace for discovering, reviewing and distributing Red-XAI software.
features: A catalog, publisher listings, review workflows and signed .rarxai packages.
Developer teams, accounts, moderation, approvals and versioned Terms acceptance.
A web store, desktop launcher integration and browser extension.
Connections to RedX workspaces and GenDragoon storage through explicit app consent.
requirements: The store service and trusted release/signing infrastructure must be provisioned before public distribution.
limitations: Coming soon to this store. Product features and supported platforms will be confirmed with its public release.
Purchases and publisher enrollment will open when the store launches.
Pricing and included entitlements will be shown before purchase.
gettingStarted: Read the product documentation.
At launch, use your Red-XAI account to browse compatible software.
Follow the supported installer and package-verification flow for the selected application.

products.name: Rotten Core
products.summary: Installation, update and application-management tools for the Red-XAI ecosystem.
features: Detect package origin from embedded/sidecar manifests and release metadata.
Verify SHA-256 checksums before installation; a mismatch refuses installation.
Install supported .app, .dmg, .pkg and .zip packages on macOS.
Maintain an installed-app inventory, check for updates and uninstall managed applications.
Expose the engine through the rottencore CLI and a Swift integration kit.
The companion RottenCoreApp repository contains an application UI for signing and installing apps.
requirements: The documented installer engine targets macOS 12 or later, Apple silicon and Intel.
Building/signing an application depends on that application’s native toolchain; the installer engine is not proof of a general-purpose build service.
limitations: Coming soon to this store.
Installation packages, signing status and supported platforms will be listed for each published release.
The companion builder interface is being prepared for public availability.
gettingStarted: Review supported package formats and system requirements.
Select an approved package and inspect its source/checksum information.
Install, check for updates or uninstall through Rotten Core when distribution opens.

products.name: Poison Apple Launcher
products.summary: A desktop library and launch experience for Rotten Apple applications.
features: Verify signed .rarxai packages and supported review/status receipts.
Install applications, maintain a local library and launch installed apps.
Refresh supported revocation/status information for managed builds.
Provide application splash screens, window controls and selectable appearance styles.
Connect applications to approved RedX data workspaces and supported GenDragoon flows.
requirements: Launcher source is part of RottenApple rather than a separately verified Poison Apple repository.
Native shell availability and signing must be checked for each release/platform.
limitations: Coming soon to this store.
Desktop platform availability will be confirmed with published installation packages.
The launcher does not itself grant accounts access to another user’s data, device or subscription.
gettingStarted: Create or use your own Red-XAI account when the launcher is distributed.
Install the supported launcher build for your platform.
Approve a supported app installation and manage it from your library.

products.name: Red-XAI DB Local
products.summary: Run the custom RedX database and BoxQL workspace on your own computer.
features: Preserve RedX’s native Box file formats and BoxQL query grammar.
Use redxd as a local REST/WebSocket database host and redx as the command-line client.
Explore data and run BoxQL through the native web console.
Use scoped API keys with database/path restrictions, expiry, rotation and auditing.
Use native write-ahead logging, checkpoints, TTLs and supported backup/restore operations.
Connect approved apps and JavaScript/Python clients; configure leader/follower replication where needed.
requirements: Release binaries target Windows, macOS, Linux and supported ARM platforms.
Source builds require Go 1.22 or later according to the repository documentation.
Advanced client keys are optional for website navigation; a standalone local host has its own explicit setup/security model.
limitations: Coming soon to this store.
Asynchronous replication is not quorum durability or automatic failover.
Local disk encryption is separate from supported pack encryption.
Per-platform signing, real installation tests and release-specific limitations must be checked.
gettingStarted: Obtain and verify an official release for your platform.
Start a local redxd host and complete its supported initial setup.
Use the local console, native redx CLI or SDK; keep local credentials private.
Back up native data before upgrades or migrations.

products.name: Red-XAI Host Local
products.summary: Run a hosting control panel and connect your own computers or VPS workers.
features: Manage projects, nodes, deployments, domains, build jobs and usage.
Start with a local SQLite control plane, built-in worker and local ZIP bundle storage.
Run supported static, Node.js, Bun, Python and custom workloads; Docker is used for workloads that require it.
Connect additional authorized workers using scoped enrollment tokens.
Configure optional Cloudflare tunnels, GitHub deployment workflows and supported registrar integrations.
Require a workload to listen on its configured port before marking deployment successful.
requirements: The documented local setup uses Bun.
Worker/runtime requirements depend on the projects you choose to run.
The control panel schedules workloads onto connected devices; it is not itself a promise of included VPS capacity.
limitations: Coming soon to this store.
Cloud providers, registrars, code signing, hosted plans and third-party integrations require separate configuration/entitlements.
Self-hosted installations require their own initial setup and explicit device enrollment.
gettingStarted: Install the documented local prerequisites.
Run the supported self-host setup flow in a trusted checkout or verified future installer.
Enroll only devices you control, then create and deploy a project.
Configure optional domains and external integrations from Host settings.

products.name: Red-XAI Bridge
products.summary: Connect approved AI clients to your own desktop through a permission-controlled MCP gateway.
features: Pair clients independently and grant only approved capabilities and folders.
Provide supported file, terminal, screenshot, application, pointer and keyboard tools.
Use Deny, Ask and Always Allow controls, client revocation and an emergency stop.
Manage approved background jobs while the desktop application remains running.
Connect supported local clients or an explicitly approved private HTTPS endpoint.
Update packaged desktop builds through public verified releases.
requirements: Windows requires an interactive signed-in desktop.
macOS requires the relevant Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.
Linux global input currently requires X11 and xdotool; Wayland input support is limited.
Each installation owns its own endpoint and pairing approvals.
limitations: Coming soon to this software store; separate public desktop releases already exist.
Bridge is not an OS sandbox and cannot bypass UAC, protected desktops or OS privacy permissions.
The latest verified stable release is 0.10.19 with Windows/Linux assets; no macOS installer is present on that release.
A public product listing does not grant universal access to anyone’s computer.
gettingStarted: Choose a verified supported desktop release.
Open Bridge, check the gateway and grant OS permissions when appropriate.
Pair a client and approve only its required capabilities.
For remote access, use this computer’s own verified HTTPS MCP URL and OAuth approval.

products.name: QuickLaunch
products.summary: Prepare software packages and publisher submissions for Rotten Apple.
features: Inspect supported applications and build signed .rarxai packages.
Register supported publishing devices and upload resumably.
Prepare store listings, submit builds and track review eligibility.
Record supported invited-tester sessions and show progress toward review requirements.
Manage encrypted local development secrets and scoped localhost tool integrations.
Provide a Go engine/CLI, local service, desktop UI and browser extension code.
requirements: Go source builds require the sibling RottenApple and RedX modules described in its README.
Native signing and platform builds depend on the appropriate operating-system toolchain.
The local service is loopback-only and token-gated.
limitations: Coming soon to this store.
Store publication and purchases will open with supported public services; no preview price is a purchase offer.
Supported platforms and installation packages will be confirmed for each release.
A separate CLI/API credential is not a website login requirement.
gettingStarted: Read the platform and signing requirements.
Inspect a supported application.
Package it using the correct platform/device signing workflow.
Submit the listing/build through the authenticated publisher workflow when the store opens.

products.name: GenDragoon Cloud SSD
products.summary: Use your own Google Cloud storage through managed upload, restore and application-cache workflows.
features: Upload files, folders and applications with verified read-back.
Restore protected copies; optionally remove a local original only after explicit verified transfer.
Launch supported applications through a local cache with bounded preloading.
Preview folder cleanup with an undo journal.
Manage accounts, projects, storage/performance plans and server-verified billing integrations.
Use available native/mobile client code and Python/JavaScript storage SDKs.
requirements: A configured storage backend, authorized account and Google Cloud resources are required.
Native platform requirements differ across macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux.
A cloud-backed cache does not have the latency or offline behavior of a physical local SSD.
limitations: Coming soon to this store.
Prebuilt release notes and checksums must be checked for signing and test-build status.
Paid storage/performance plans are not included merely by downloading a client.
Native/mobile availability is release-specific.
gettingStarted: Review supported client/platform behavior.
Connect your own authenticated account and storage project.
Test upload and restore with disposable data.
Use verified transfer status before choosing any optional local cleanup.

products.name: Red-XAI Hub
products.summary: A planned unified home for Red-XAI products, account tools and services.
features: Discover Red-XAI products and documentation in one place.
Open account-scoped Host and DB tools from a shared Hub.
Read announcements, updates and service information.
Reach account settings, developer documentation and future community features.
requirements: The verified existing Hub is website source inside Red-XAIHost-8612.
A distinct downloadable Red-XAI Hub application and its installer have not been found in the connected repositories.
limitations: Coming soon to this software store.
This entry describes the planned Hub product; it does not advertise an existing standalone desktop/mobile download.
The community portal is a separate destination and is also coming soon.
gettingStarted: Use your existing website account.
Explore the Hub’s product catalog and documentation.
Open only the services and resources assigned to your own account.

products.name: Red-SecretsXAI
products.summary: An encryption toolkit with a shared native core, language bindings and red-X PNG containers.
features: Documented password and port/keymap workflows for files, folders, application bundles and supported drive images.
A shared C++ core with Python, C++, C#, Java and JavaScript bindings.
Authenticated streamed encryption, documented recovery and key-card workflows.
Red-X PNG conversion with error-correction features.
A public documentation site and language/CLI guides.
requirements: Requirements depend on the selected binding; the public install guide documents Python 3.10+, Node.js 18+, .NET 8, JDK 21 and C++17 paths.
Current published package versions and native platform assets must be checked separately from the documentation snapshot.
limitations: Free listing as requested. The implementation repository is currently private; this page does not change its visibility or grant source access.
Public documentation is available and describes a reviewed 0.3.1 snapshot.
The project is pre-audit. Feature descriptions are not a claim of independent cryptographic certification.
Do not advertise all registry/package versions as publicly available based only on README installation examples.
gettingStarted: Start with the public installation/access guide.
Choose a supported language binding and confirm the package version.
Practice seal/open/recovery using disposable files.
Keep recovery material offline and follow the public security documentation.

products.name: REDXAI CLI
products.summary: Command-line access to supported Red-XAI installation, update and service workflows.
features: Published stable 0.3.0: download/install supported Bridge builds and update the CLI.
Verify downloaded assets against release checksums, size and GitHub digests where available.
Both REDXAI and redxai executable aliases are packaged.
Published opt-in 0.4.0 manual preview: account-based DB/Host browser entry points, optional scoped-key scripting and supported device-node lifecycle commands.
requirements: Node.js 20 or later and npm.
A user-writable installation location; no administrator rights are required for a per-user prefix.
Host node requirements depend on the selected operating system and workload.
The optional manual preview uses its bundled setup toolkit and a separate redxai-candidate command; Node.js 20+ must already be installed.
limitations: Free as requested.
The verified public stable download is an OS-neutral .tgz package, not a native .exe, .dmg or Linux graphical installer.
DB, Host and node commands are available in the public 0.4.0 manual preview; they are not included in stable 0.3.0.
Use the linked release package and manual instructions; registry and Homebrew installation are not currently offered here.
Bridge installation requires a compatible published asset for the selected operating system; the CLI does not supply a missing Bridge build.
The preview includes manual toolkits, not GUI installers. Signing/notarization, real user-profile installation and physical-device lifecycle acceptance remain unfinished.
No unrestricted persistent iPhone hosting node is shipped.
gettingStarted: Download the verified CLI package and confirm its SHA-256.
Install into your own user prefix using npm with lifecycle scripts disabled.
Open a new terminal or add the prefix to your session PATH.
Run redxai version and redxai help; use only commands documented for your installed version.
To try DB/Host/node commands, download the matching public manual preview toolkit, verify its checksum and follow its bundled INSTALL.md.
Opt into the separate redxai-candidate command when wanted; the preview preserves existing stable REDXAI/redxai installations and does not enroll a Host node automatically.
